root_causes.root_cause: RFC-029 D2 added suspect_density check to validate_tree (chars_per_page < 1500 floor with page_count threading). For warid-597 (42-page scanned Arabic PDF, 54728 chars / 42 pages = 1303 chars/page < 1500), this fires and returns (False, 'suspect_density'). But 'suspect_density' is not handled by ANY recovery or routing path in client.py -- not in OCR escalation triggers (garbling/node_garbling/visual_order_garble), not in flat routing (node_count<3/depth<2), not in VLM fallback. Falls through to LowQualityTreeError raise at line 1639. In Run 12, the tree PASSED validate_tree (garble gate blind to numeric-junk) and was persisted. RFC-029 design intended verdict change to MARGINAL/FAIL, not ERROR.
root_causes.code_path: helpers.py:validate_tree (line 1359-1365) -> client.py (line 1381-1387, reason not in flat routing set) -> client.py (line 1637-1639, raises LowQualityTreeError)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add 'suspect_density' (and other new RFC-029 validate_tree reasons: 'arabic_low_content_ratio', 'low_content_density', 'empty_node_contamination') to the flat routing path's reason check at client.py line 1387. Change: reason in ('node_count<3', 'depth<2') to include these new reasons. This routes rejected trees to flat extraction (which matches RFC-029 D1 design intent) instead of raising LowQualityTreeError. Alternatively, move the suspect_density check from validate_tree to classify_verdict so the tree is persisted but gets a lower verdict.
